title: GRT bus advertising referred to budget process
subtitle: Downtown Kitchener Duke Street cycle tracks recommended; New Dundee official plan amendment for six lots recommended.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee spent most of its meeting on proposed changes to Grand River Transit advertising rules. Staff proposed raising the cap on fully wrapped buses from five to 10% of the fleet, allowing Region-led information campaigns on buses, and wrapping one ION train. The committee instead recommended sending the report back to staff for the 2024 budget process, with public consultation as part of budget talks. It also recommended continuing the Truth and Reconciliation bus wrap until February 29, 2024 {{vote:m4}}.

The committee recommended approving a physically separated two-way cycle track on the west side of Duke Street in downtown Kitchener between Francis and Water streets. The short section from Frederick to Water Street will be revisited as part of the integrated mobility plan, and staff will report back {{vote:m5}}.

On the consent agenda, the committee recommended a site-specific Regional Official Plan amendment for 63 Benjamin Street in New Dundee. It would allow up to six lots using tertiary wastewater treatment systems {{vote:m1}}. Residents will see final decisions when Council considers these recommendations.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended referring the report back to staff for consideration before final 2024 budget day on December 13, 2023, with consultation included in the budget process.
The committee recommended that Region information campaigns not count toward the bus wrap limit, and that a funding source and process be identified.
The committee amended the motion to continue the Truth and Reconciliation bus wrap until February 29, 2024, and to refer to "Regional information campaigns" {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended the design of separated two-way cycle tracks on the west side of Duke Street between Francis and Water streets, with the Frederick to Water section revisited in the integrated mobility plan.
The committee recommended adopting a Regional Official Plan amendment allowing up to six lots using tertiary wastewater treatment, and directed staff to prepare the implementing by-law.

debate: A delegate opposed more wraps, arguing they weaken GRT and ION branding, make transit rides worse because windows are covered, and that the report offered no analysis of ridership effects.

Several councillors said they were surprised by the public reaction and that there had been no community consultation. They preferred referral to the budget process, where residents could weigh the revenue against other priorities. Staff said they had no major concern with referral, but needed a decision on the Truth and Reconciliation wrap before the end of October.

Many councillors opposed wrapping an ION train, calling it a signature regional brand. Staff estimated the train and about 20 more buses would bring similar revenue. Some councillors were open to more buses.

Councillors questioned what "social initiatives" meant and who would choose them. Staff clarified the intent was Region-led campaigns, and the wording was narrowed to Regional information campaigns. Some raised accessibility, noting wrapped windows are harder to see through, and asked who would fund such wraps.

On Duke Street, staff said they could not fit two-way buses and two-way cycling in the narrow section between Water and Frederick streets. Diverting buses would reduce ridership and raise costs. A councillor asked that the church on that block be kept informed, and another asked that the section be revisited rather than left open-ended.
